newsitem.title: USA: Perot to file lawsuit on debate Monday.
newsitem.headline: Perot to file lawsuit on debate Monday.

text.p: Ross Perot's Reform Party said Saturday it will file a lawsuit Monday seeking an injunction against the Commission on Presidential Debates' if the Texas billionaire is not permitted to participate in the presidential debates.
The commission last week recommended excluding Perot and his running mate Pat Choate, saying they did not have a realistic chance of winning the election.
Negotiators for President Clinton and Republican candidate Bob Dole agreed Saturday to hold two presidential and one vice presidential debate and to exclude the Reform Party candidates.
The Perot campaign said its lawsuit would be filed at 11 a.m. EDT in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., with a news conference planned shortly thereafter.

"The lawsuit is being filed because the commission based its decision on subjective criteria, not on the objective criteria which both Mr. Perot, Dr. Choate and the Reform Party meet," the campaign said in a statement.
Attorney Jamin Raskin said the lawsuit argued that constitutional guarantees of free speech and equal protection should oblige courts to overrule the commission.
"Courts have regularly struck down rules which say that incumbents get favoured positions on the ballots," he said. "This is the same kind of stacking of the deck against minor party candidates."
Perot's campaign lodged a formal complaint on Friday with the Federal Election Commission, which oversees political campaign spending, taking aim at the commission.

The complaint alleges that the debate commission has broken the law by disregarding an FEC rule stipulating that the commission must use objective criteria in deciding who is eligible to participate in presidential debates. It is also forbidden to use nomination by a particular party as a standard for inclusion.

The Clinton team had pushed for inclusion of the Reform Party candidates, but Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor Saturday said the Dole camp insisted it would not participate in the debates at all if Perot and Choate were included.
